definition: Emulate means to imitate someone in an effort to match and eventually surpass them.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word emulate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know emulate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The young cartoonist taped her favorite artist's strips above her desk, hoping first to emulate his comic timing and someday to out-draw him.
Copying reproduces the surface - the answers, the brushstrokes; emulate reaches past the surface toward the model's whole achievement.
Imitating follows someone's example; emulate goes further, following it with the declared aim of matching or beating it.

To mirror something is to reflect it exactly - the tribute set matches the original note for note, adding nothing of its own. Emulate follows a model with ambition attached: you copy in order to catch up, meaning one day to surpass. A mirror never overtakes what it reflects.

To rival someone is to match or challenge them - two bakeries can rival each other without either studying the other. Emulate starts from admiration: you take a model, follow it closely, and work to equal or surpass it. Rivals simply compete; emulators first apprentice themselves.
to deliberately avoid, rather than follow
to refuse to accept as a model
Emulate comes from Latin aemulus, 'rival.' Apart from its own noun, emulation, the root produced no other common English word, so the family tree stops here.
Emulate means to imitate someone in an effort to match and eventually surpass them.
Teo emulated his older sister in everything: when she made the honor roll, he aimed for valedictorian; when she built a robot for the science fair, he built two.
He wasn't copying her so much as racing her.
Emulate is more ambitious than imitate: both start by following a model, but emulate adds the goal of equaling or surpassing it.
You imitate a birdcall; you emulate a hero.
Emulate is the word for imitation with ambition: you follow a model because you mean to match or surpass it.
Plain imitate or copy stops at reproduction.
Among this unit's drive words, emulate names where the drive points - at a person ahead of you - while resolute and zealous describe the firmness and heat you bring to the chase.

At sixteen, Amara Sy took the bus across Dakar every Sunday just to stand in line at Maison Keita, the bakery every critic called untouchable.

When she opened her own shop years later, she made no secret of her plan to emulate it: she learned Keita's canonical loaves one by one, kept his dawn schedule, even adopted his habit of numbering every batch.
'You start by walking in the master's footprints,' she told an apprentice.

'You do it so exactly that one day the footprints end -- and you keep walking.' Critics noticed the homage first, then the divergence: her rye held Keita's crust but a darker crumb, her mornings ran earlier than his.
Last spring, for the first time, a national guide ranked her shop above the one she had once crossed the city to admire.
